Conversation.line: I wonder if we'll find anything interesting in the ruins this time?
Like your own death?
Well, or someone else's.
If we find any ruins at all.
They may not be on our way.
Here's what I thought...
Oh no. Someone started to think. We're done.
Very funny.
... And what if we throw this joker overboard?
They don't appreciate my subtle nature here...
... Why didn't we get these jellies earlier when disassembling artifacts in the deconstructor?
The deconstructor has a special program for disassembling things.
And, since no one knew about the existence of the jelly before, these huge, motionless sharp blades simply cut the artifacts into three alien materials, without considering the rest.
In other words, you don't know, do you?
Good question.
Let's put the question differently - does anyone even know how a deconstructor works?
Well, actually... I have no idea.
... Why does the crawler matriarch have breasts?
No more pouring for him!
To distract predators who will look at it while she bites off their heads.
Quite an interesting anatomical feature, by the way. Crawler are probably much closer to humans than we thought.
Some questions are best left unanswered.
... What are these guardians of the ruins?
Well, you would also ask how artifacts work, with a detailed explanation. Hell knows.
Only at research stations will be able to answer for sure.
Judging by what I saw during the forays into the ruins - something like a huge pile of electronics in a shell resembling a spacesuit.
... Why haven't we found all these new artifacts before?
Hell knows.
They were just actively hiding, and now that we have thermal visor technology, they don't stand a chance.
Only research stations will be able to answer for sure.
Good question.
We still know too little to be sure.
